description:
FILED s470bq (Opus, 2026-09-05) as the DECLARED residue of #1213, and stated
in docs/ir-spec.md Â§12c so a reader of the spec sees the boundary.

`pl2cl --facts` wraps ten licences.  The rest of the registry is not wrapped,
and the reason is structural rather than an omission: their licence is not a
local choice between two emitted forms.  It is a DECLARATION's CLASS, which is
already in the IR as `p-let`'s `:class` and facts tail (#1035, ir-spec
Â§2b.2a).  Under `PCL_OPT=none` the class prints `:box`, and what `--facts`
would have to add is what the class WOULD have been -- which means running the
verdict even with the switch off and carrying the answer to the declaration
site.  That is VarAnnotator plumbing, not a wrapper.

`numeric-slot` is the boundary case and is instructive: it IS wired, but its
site is only reached because `raw-slot` fired, so it is absent under
`PCL_OPT=none` while every other wired licence is present.  The gate row in
Pl/t/ir-data-form-01.t therefore compares the nine switch-independent names,
and names numeric-slot's exception in a comment.

`dyn-loop-exit` is separate again: its OFF arm is a die at the exit site, not
a general form, so there is nothing to wrap.

WHAT TO DO: give VarAnnotator's verdicts a "would have fired" channel that
survives the Kind-A gate (the shape already exists once -- #1213 added
`foreach_ro_fact` beside `foreach_ro` for exactly this), then carry it to
`_decl_entry` so the declaration can wear `(p-fact (raw-numeric :num) â¦)`.
Bar: emission IDENTICAL without `--facts` (corpus-diff), and the licence
counts equal between `--facts` and `PCL_OPT=none --facts` for the whole
registry.
subject: --facts does not cover the verdict-COVERAGE licences (raw-slot / raw-numeric / str-buffer / the three narrowings / raw-return-family / dyn-loop-exit)
